newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trade flattened by fee protest.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trade flattened by fee protest.

text.p: A row over the introduction of a new transaction fee flattened Wednesday trading on the Nigerian stock exchange.
The all-share index closed at 6535.00 from 6524.18 on Tuesday.
Most stockbrokers joined the protest over a half percent fee which the stock exchange was now demanding on all transactions, saying it would be a disincentive to investors.
Only 28 deals were recorded compared to 150 on Tuesday.
Last month the stock exchange said it was reducing transaction fees to encourage investment, but at the same time introduced the new charge on stockbrokers.

"We thought the fee was still under discussion and then they sprung this on us today. Are we supposed to be lowering costs or increasing them? We don't know what the exchange is up to," said one trader.
A meeting between brokers and the exchange is to take place on Thursday to try and resolve the dispute.
Only seven shares moved, all of them rising.
Guinness which has recently been on the slide closed 20 kobo up at 8.85 naira.
Ashaka Cement gained 50 kobo to 18.50 naira.
Insurance firm AIICO closed up nine kobo at 7.00 naira. Niger Insurance closed five kobo higher at 2.40 naira.
Trade Bank rose five kobo to 1.90 naira.
